question: In an interview with the ‘Rynek Zdrowia’ portal, published on the ‘Kanal Gospodarczy’ channel on YouTube on 17 February 2026, Polish Health Minister Jolanta SobierańskaGrenda stated: ‘For several years, the European Commission has been indicating that there are too many hospital beds in Poland’.

1 2 This statement was made in response to questions about the allegedly excessive number of hospitals in Poland, the scope of medical services provided in them, and the ongoing crisis in Polish healthcare. In light of the above: 1.

Is it true, as Minister Sobierańska-Grenda claims, that ‘the European Commission has been indicating that there are too many hospital beds in Poland’, which consequently means too many hospitals and too many medical services provided in them? If so, in which documents drafted by the Commission can such conclusions be found?

If the above statement is true, on what grounds are Commission representatives voicing their opinions on the organisation of the healthcare system in Poland, given that, under the Treaties, EU actions can only be complementary to national health policies and mainly serve to support them?

Is the Commission aware that maternity wards in Poland are being closed at an unprecedented rate, with 18 being closed in January 2026 alone, and that rules have been introduced allowing births to be handled by hospitals without maternity wards – for instance, in emergency wards? Are these measures being taken as a consequence of the Commission’s aforementioned recommendations to reduce the number of hospital beds?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.4.2026) According to Article 168(7) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union1, Member States are responsible for organising and delivering health services and medical care. The EU supports Member States with tools and initiatives such as technical assistance, knowledge sharing, funding and policy guidance.

The European Semester provides a framework to identify and address policy challenges in Member States, ensuring coordination at EU level while safeguarding the principle of subsidiarity. The latest European Semester Polish country report’s health annex2 shows that Poland’s health system is comparatively hospital-centred. Poland had one of the highest numbers of hospital beds per 1000 population in 2023, 6.3 vs 5.

1 for the EU, with concurrent low occupancy rates. However, Poland has not received a country specific recommendation regarding the closure of maternity wards. The findings in the health annex are analytical in nature and do not, in themselves, entail a recommendation to close facilities. Decisions on the organisation of hospital networks, including maternity wards, remain a national competence.
To the Commission’s knowledge, there is no direct link between analyses presented under the European Semester and the closure of maternity wards in Poland as raised by the Honourable Member.
